The oscillating spheroidal charge distribution has a time-varying electric quadrupole moment (since its shape oscillates while the center of charge remains fixed). Electric quadrupole radiation has a power per unit solid angle proportional to \(\sin^2\theta \cos^2\theta\) and scales with wavelength as \(\lambda^{-6}\). The maximum of \(\sin^2\theta \cos^2\theta\) occurs at \(\theta = 45^\circ\) with value \(1/4\). At \(\theta = 30^\circ\), the value is \(\sin^2 30^\circ \cos^2 30^\circ = (1/4)(3/4) = 3/16\). The fraction of the maximum is \((3/16)/(1/4) = 3/4\). Thus the fraction is \(3/4\) and the wavelength dependence is \(\lambda^{-6}\).

Answer: C
